2. Plaintiff Khairunnessa filed the aforesaid title suit for a declaration that she was entitled to continue as a lessee of shop No. 49 in the ground floor of Baitul Mokarram under the management of Islamic Foundation i.e. the appellant, as an heir and successor of late Md Ismail, her maternal uncle and also for a decree for permanent injunction and recovery of Khas possession of the said shop from the appellants alleging, inter alia, that her maternal uncle late Mohammad Ismail took a lease of the said shop from the Baitul Mokarram Managing Committee in the year 1960 and carried on business of selling guns there under the business name Calcutta Gun Repairing Works. Subsequently, the name was changed from "Calcutta Gun Repairing Works" to "East Pakistan Small Arms" and the authority concerned was requested for correcting their record accordingly. Since the Baitul Mokarram Managing Committee did not care to change their record in this regard the former business name "Calcutta Gun Repairing Works continued on the record of the said managing committee of Baitul Mokarram. Late Mohammad Ismail disappeared while he was going from Mohammadpur to Mirpur along with his family members on the 24th December, 1971 and it was subsequently known that he was killed along with his family members by miscreants on that date and since then he was not heard of by any of his relations. In the circumstances one Ayesha Begum, the only sister of Md Ismail was alive and living at her residence at 9, Shirish Das Lane, Sutrapur, Dhaka, Hence in the absence of Md Ismail said Ayesha Begum as the sole heir of Ismail used to carry on business at the said shop by appointing employees. Thereafter, the said Ayesha Begum died of cancer on 4-6-77 at Khulna leaving behind her only daughter i.e. the plaintiff Khairunnessa. In 1975 Baitul Mokarram Committee was dissolved and Islamic Foundation i.e. the present appellant was constituted and since then the said Islamic Foundation has been looking after the affairs of the Baitul Mokarram. After the death of Ayesha Begum, plaintiff Khairunnessa as the sole heir of Ayesha Begum was entitled to continue the said business at the aforesaid shop as a lessee under the Islamic Foundation. But the Islamic Foundation i.e. the appellant took over possession of the said shop after the death of Ayesha Begum and refused to hand over the same in favour of the plaintiff Khairunnessa. Plaintiff Khairunnessa requested the appellant Islamic Foundation to hand over possession of the said shop but that was lastly refused by the appellant on 11-2-88 and, as a result, she was constrained to file the present suit. 

 (6) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to recovery of khas possession as well as permanent injunction in respect of the suit property?
